messages:
maria: quick q — for audit downloads we currently generate presigned S3 links valid 7 days. for regulated customers should we: A) extend to 30d, B) store a signed artifact in cold storage and return a stable internal link, or C) require a manual legal-hold workflow? also need to capture who actually downloaded the file in our audit events. thoughts?

 taylor: i'm leaning toward short-lived presigned links + storing an immutable copy in cold storage for e-discovery. presigned 7d is fine as default. for enterprise customers offer an opt-in 'preserve' flag that copies the artifact to cold storage with retention and legal-hold controls.

 jonathan: +1 but we need telemetry to distinguish "link created" vs "file downloaded" vs "link expired". compliance teams ask for the access chain. events should include actor id, token id, ip, user-agent. we also need a way to later prove the artifact contents (hash). PII redaction policy still TBD.

 ravi: agree. also put tenant-level rate-limits on downloads — otherwise someone can script downloads and spike egress costs. suggestion: allow limiting downloads per-link and per-tenant, and optionally issue one-time download nonces.

 compliance-bot: note: preservation/ediscovery requests require a provable chain. storing a signed artifact makes that chain simpler; presigned links are convenient but fragile if bucket policies change.

 maria: two sub-questions: 1) telemetry schema for those events, 2) console UX for showing link state (valid until, downloads, who). For telemetry i'm thinking three new events: audit.export_link.created, audit.export_link.downloaded, audit.export_link.expired. ideally include a download_proof_id returned to the caller on successful download.

 taylor: rough minimal telemetry sketch:
 ```
 {
  "event": "audit.export_link.downloaded",
  "tenant_id": "T-123",
  "actor": "user:alice@example.com",
  "artifact_id": "a-456",
  "link_id": "l-789",
  "action": "download",
  "timestamp": "2024-04-10T15:22:33Z",
  "ip": "1.2.3.4",
  "ua": "curl/7.85",
  "bytes": 452345
 }
 ```
 We should mark which fields are sensitive (actor, ip) and route to pii-protected streams. Also store file_hash at creation time so we can later verify integrity.

 jonathan: for PII we can store hashed actor email in the general telemetry, with raw stored only in a secure audit store accessible via compliance playbooks. retention windows differ per-tenant. maybe HSM for keys used to hash.

 ravi: console UX: download modal should show: "link valid until X", "downloaded N times", "last downloaded by Y (masked) at T" and actions: "revoke link", "regenerate link", "preserve artifact (legal hold)". add small note about retention and who can access the preserved copy.

 maria: API implications: POST /audit/exports -> returns {artifact_id, link_id, presigned_url, expires_at}. Add optional ?preserve=true or body {preserve:true} to create/stage permanent artifact. GET /audit/exports/:id/downloads -> paginated list of download events. POST /audit/exports/:id/revoke to invalidate existing links.

 taylor: security notes: presigned URLs signed with ephemeral key, default TTL=7d. if preserve=true -> copy to cold store and return only an internal stable artifact_id; public presigned link can be generated on demand and will be short-lived. RBAC check required to create a public link when preserve is true.

 jonathan: telemetry detail: include correlation_id that ties export creation -> link create -> download events. also include file_hash (sha256) at creation to enable later integrity checks and to prove evidence hasn't changed. store file_hash in the audit ledger.

 maria: proposed decision (quick): default behavior remains presigned 7d links; add enterprise opt-in preserve=true which stores a signed artifact with long retention and legal hold; emit three telemetry events (created/downloaded/expired) with a download_proof_id and file_hash; console shows link metadata and exposes revoke/regenerate/preserve actions; add tenant-level download rate-limits and optional one-time nonces. action items: @taylor draft telemetry schema PR, @jonathan prototype download rate-limit + nonce, @ravi mock modal for console. i'll open an RFC this afternoon.

 taylor: ack — i'll draft PR by EOD Thurs.

 jonathan: i'll do rate-limit prototype tomorrow morning.

 ravi: mock ready for design review next Tue.

 deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: audit-service v1.22 -> canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

 maria: thanks all :thumbsup:
